security_goal: Detect observable divergence between a consumer-visible SBI representation and a nearby trusted reference representation when the attacker cannot control the reference or detector.

trust_levels.name: Experimental evaluation integrity
trust_levels.claim: Private attack labels are unavailable to the blind detector and are joined only after detection.

trust_levels.name: Post-common-path branch integrity
trust_levels.claim: Current live Open5GS validation: native NRF and SCP are trusted common infrastructure; the adversary can modify only the consumer-facing copy after the genuine SCP->NRF transaction.

trust_levels.name: Independent-observer node-compromise model
trust_levels.claim: Target framework: a compromised reporting node may lie, but at least one comparison observation must be generated outside that node's control.

trust_levels.name: Multi-point Byzantine/common-mode compromise
trust_levels.claim: Attacker controls both report and trusted reference, or controls common infrastructure feeding both observations.

assumptions.text: Native Open5GS NRF and SCP binaries are not modified or compromised in the Stage-21 live experiment.
The attacker cannot alter the trusted-reference request, its response after the trusted observation point, or detector state.

The consumer and reference requests may observe benign temporal differences because they are separate nearby requests; stability gating is used to avoid treating volatile paths as trusted semantic invariants.
The research attacker may choose sparse or persistent payload mutations on the consumer branch, including value substitution, field deletion and profile removal.
No collusion or simultaneous compromise of both the consumer branch and trusted-reference branch is assumed.
Deterministic SHA-256 semantic tokens are equality tokens only; they are not message authentication codes and no privacy guarantee is claimed.
Label separation is an experimental-validity property, not an operational security mechanism.

observability_condition.statement: An attack is observable only if it creates a difference in at least one enabled monitored representation between trusted reference and consumer view, and the corresponding frozen sequential rule reaches its alarm condition.
observability_condition.common_mode_failure: If both observations contain the same false state, pairwise reconciliation alone cannot establish that the common state is false.
observability_condition.representation_invariance_failure: If the attacker changes semantics while preserving all monitored representations, the detector cannot observe that change.

tested_attack_classes.class: cross-profile identity swap preserving normalized per-path value multiset

out_of_scope_or_not_established: Compromise of native Open5GS SCP itself
Compromise of NRF or any other common source that can make reference and consumer views identically false
Compromise of the trusted reference collector
Collusion between compromised reporting and reference points
Production mutual-TLS, OAuth and SEPP trust chains
Arbitrary transport denial-of-service and timing attacks
Relational/cross-entity semantics preserved by per-path multiset projections
Truth of the underlying network state when both paired observations agree

claim_boundary.allowed: Stage 21 validates detection of consumer-branch integrity divergence after a genuine native Open5GS SCP->NRF path under a trusted-reference assumption.
claim_boundary.forbidden_overclaim: Stage 21 proves detection of a compromised native SCP, compromised NRF, or arbitrary Byzantine multi-point attacker.
